clue.text: Excuse the friendly sounding crew

annotationWithheld.why: Excuse the friendly sounding crew (8): PALLY (friendly) + EIGHT (crew) said aloud, but the indicator 'sounding' stands between the two words heard, so no single leaf can hold the heard run and the grammar cannot express one homophone over both

clue.text: In here a rod for this mischievous child ?

definitions.text: In here a rod for this mischievous child ?

parts.words: In here a rod for this mischievous child ?
parts.note: a punishment kept ready; the same word is an old name for an impish youngster

explanation.surface: A cane is kept handy for punishing a naughty youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To have a rod in pickle' means to keep a punishment waiting for someone; the container holding the rod is also a word for a little rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is an old affectionate term for a naughty child, and a rod soaked in brine is the punishment saved for one.

clue.text: Ship includes a kind of accelerator

indicators.note: includes shows the vessel word holding the next piece inside it

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A vessel carries some sort of speed-boosting device on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A linear accelerator speeds particles along a straight track, so this is a type of particle accelerator.

clue.text: Apprentice in the upper set perhaps

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth, such as an upper plate

explanation.surface: A trainee belongs to the top social class, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper set' suggests high society, but it is a set of false teeth for the top jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To indenture someone is to bind them by contract as an apprentice; both words are verbs here.

clue.text: One vessel being the lighter, following this

definitions.text: One vessel being the lighter, following this

parts.words: One vessel being the lighter, following this
parts.note: cargo moved from a ship to another craft, such as a lighter barge, has undergone this process

explanation.surface: Seems to compare two boats, one less heavily laden.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships, not a comparison of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means transferring goods from one ship to another vessel, as when a lighter takes cargo off.

clue.text: One Carlist leader in pursuit of a champion (Spanish) tart

indicators.note: in pursuit of puts the following pieces after the earlier ones, chasing them

parts.note: El Cid was the great Spanish champion of medieval legend
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the leader of Carlist is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Spanish Carlist chief chases a champion and turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlists were supporters of a rival Spanish royal line in the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic food has a sharp, sour taste, which is what tart describes.

clue.text: How to secure a pile?

definitions.meaning: to fasten firmly with a gripping tool
a heap of potatoes stored under earth, or a stack of bricks for firing

explanation.definitionFit: To clamp something is to fix it tight, and a clamp is also a stored heap of root crops or bricks.

clue.text: Bird sues for damages, we have to pay out

indicators.note: damages here means wreckage, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A man called Bird sues for compensation and we must foot the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sues for damages' reads as a lawsuit, but 'for damages' signals that BIRD SUES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburse money is to spend or pay it out from a fund.

clue.text: Fellows are upper house Marxists ?

parts.note: Com is short for Communist, a follower of Marx
the House of Lords is made up of peers

explanation.surface: Asks whether the House of Lords is full of communists.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'upper house Marxists' as Communist members of the Lords: COM followed by PEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is an equal or companion, so the plural means fellows or comrades.

clue.text: American half died in the promised land

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the name of the land

parts.note: Canaan is the land promised to the Israelites in the Bible

indicators.note: half of died is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone from the US died halfway into reaching paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaan is the land God promised to Abraham's descendants; the American here comes from north of the US border.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is in North America, so a Canadian is a North American, if not from the United States.

clue.text: Get money back for somebody ? On the contrary

definitions.text: Get money back for somebody ? On the contrary

parts.words: Get money back for somebody ? On the contrary
parts.note: turn the phrase round: get somebody back in return for money, the payment a kidnapper demands

explanation.surface: Seems to be about claiming a refund on someone's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' tells you to swap 'money' and 'somebody': a payment that gets a captive back.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper's demand is a sum paid to secure the release of a hostage.

clue.text: Representative element of the community appears angry

definitions.text: Representative element of the community appears angry

parts.words: Representative element of the community appears angry
parts.note: a typical sample of society, and also a part of the population that is in a bad temper

explanation.surface: A delegate group from the town turns up looking furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross means angry, so a section of society that is cross gives the phrase for a typical sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a sample that fairly represents the whole group.

clue.text: To get to know money, work for it

parts.note: L stands for a pound, from the Latin libra
to earn money is to work for it

explanation.surface: To understand money you must work for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to come to know it through study or experience.

clue.text: Source of those diabolical quotations ?

parts.note: Shakespeare says the devil can cite holy writ for his purpose, so the Bible is where the devil gets his quotes

explanation.surface: Asks where some wicked sayings come from.
explanation.walkthrough: From The Merchant of Venice: 'The devil can cite Scripture for his purpose.'
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred writings such as the Bible are what the devil is said to quote.

clue.text: Victim of a " brutal " killing

parts.note: the quotation marks hint at Brutus, one of the assassins of the Roman dictator in 44 BC

explanation.surface: Names someone murdered savagely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brutal' in quotation marks is a play on Brutus, who stabbed the Roman leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman dictator was assassinated by a group including Brutus on the Ides of March.

clue.text: Donald Duck's liveliness

definitions.meaning: Disney's cartoon duck is a product of the art of making drawn films move

explanation.definitionFit: Cartoon characters like Disney's duck are made by drawing frames in sequence, and the same word means vigour and spirit.

clue.text: Vitreous rock-foreign aid is bound to give partial backing

indicators.note: backing means the chosen run is read from right to left
partial means only part of the phrase is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Overseas aid is sure to give only half-hearted support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial' takes a run of letters from 'foreign aid is bound' and 'backing' turns that run around.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark natural glass formed from volcanic lava, a glassy rock.

clue.text: Old Bob sang as he ambled along

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
to troll is an old word for singing cheerfully

explanation.surface: Old Bob sings to himself as he wanders along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it was slang for a shilling, the coin worth 12 old pennies, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk at a leisurely pace, much like ambling.

clue.text: But school-days get us nothing in return for material

parts.note: a school term is a set period of school days

indicators.note: in return means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing or zero

explanation.surface: School days give us nothing back for our efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns NIL into LIN at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a loosely woven cotton cloth, originally used for wrapping butter, so a fabric.

clue.text: First male academician put up " Philip's fleet "

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible
RA stands for Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An early academy member presents a painting called Philip's fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ADAM + RA to give the answer; Philip II of Spain sent this fleet against England in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was the war fleet King Philip II sent to invade England.

clue.text: Fly discovered by Eliot initially, twice

indicators.note: twice says the letters are written two times over

parts.note: the poet T. S. Eliot's initials, with E for his surname

explanation.surface: An insect was spotted by the poet Eliot at first, then again.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's initials T, S and E are repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Ring a coin — could be made of such substance

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A ring or coin could be made of this material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges RING A COIN; metal used for rings and coins is not living matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Metals are not derived from living things, so they are classed as mineral rather than biological substance.

clue.text: Kind of painting

definitions.meaning: a sort or category, especially in art or writing
a style of picture showing scenes of everyday life

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a type or category, and genre painting depicts ordinary domestic scenes.

clue.text: A " rash intruding fool ' was stuck behind it

definitions.text: A " rash intruding fool ' was stuck behind it

parts.words: A " rash intruding fool ' was stuck behind it
parts.note: Hamlet calls Polonius a wretched rash intruding fool after stabbing him through the tapestry he hid behind

explanation.surface: Describes a meddler killed while hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Polonius hides behind a wall hanging and Hamlet runs him through it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a woven tapestry hung on a wall, behind which Polonius eavesdropped.

clue.text: John Bull's Shavian alternative is real property

parts.note: land is real property in law, as opposed to movable goods

explanation.surface: Seems to say that Shaw's choice for John Bull is real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's play is John Bull's Other Island, so the 'other' or alternative is the missing word of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw titled his Irish play John Bull's Other Island, the other being Ireland.

clue.text: The giddy limit, with a worker up in arms

indicators.note: giddy means dizzy and reeling, so the letters of limit are spun round

parts.note: worker ants do the labour of a colony

explanation.surface: The absolute limit: a labourer rising in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The giddy limit' is a British phrase for something outrageous, but 'giddy' rearranges LIMIT into MILIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone militant is combative and ready to fight, which is what up in arms conveys.

clue.text: Gave Homeric assent ?

parts.note: agreeing with a bob of the head, and recalling the saying that even Homer sometimes slips

explanation.surface: Asks how one agreed in epic style.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'even Homer nods' means even the best make mistakes; nodding is also how one says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping the head is a sign of agreement, and Homer was proverbially said to doze off at times.

clue.text: Flood causes antediluvian organization to suffer a £4 loss

indicators.note: organization means the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: L is the symbol for pound sterling
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Floods ruin an ancient firm, which loses four pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suffer a £4 loss' removes A, L and IV from the letters of ANTEDILUVIAN; the rest, rearranged by 'organization', give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, to swamp.
